lawyer:
Probir Neogi, Advocate with Sikder Mahmudur Razi, Advocate—For the Plaintiff-Appellants. 
Goutam Kumar Roy, Advocate with Lucky Begum, Advocate—For the Defendants-Respondents.
parties:
Syed NM Kamal being dead his legal heirs Syeda Nargis Begum and others…….Plaintiffs-Appellants
vs
Achia Khatun and others…….Defendants-Respondents
full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: This First Appeal at the instance of the plaintiff and is directed against the judgment and decree dated 15-10-2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 305 of 2003 dismissing the suit.

2. The present appellants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 305 of 2003 in the Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka impleading the respondents as defendants for declaration of title and for further declaration that the judgment and preliminary decree dated 31-7-2012 and final decree dated 26-2-2003 passed in Title Suit No. 368 of 2001 are collusive, ineffective, null and void and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

3. During pendency of the appeal Sayed NM Kamal, appellant No. 1 died and his legal heirs were duly substituted as appellant Nos. 1(a)-1(f) including his wife Mrs Hamina Beum alias Mrs Hasina Begum, who is already on record as appellant No. 2. Subsequently, appellant No.2 also died and her heirs duly substituted by order of this Court dated 12-4-2016.

4. The plaintiff case in short, is that Jozeshwar Sharma, Rajeshwar Sharma, Ratneshwar Sharma and Guneshwar Sharma were the CS recorder owners of 1.78 acres of land in CS Khatian No. 252, CS Plot Nos. 502, 503 and 504; that each of them was owner of 4 annas share in the land, while on the basis of amicable settlement, they have been possessing the respective portion of their land, Guneshwar Sharma died issueless leaving behind wife Kusum Kumari Debi as his successor and during SA survey her name was duly recorded in SA Khatian No. 307 in 4 annas share with other co-sharer and had been possessing the same for more than statutory period of limitation; that while she was in possessing of the said land due to her legal necessity, she transferred 0.1650 acres of land in plot No. 504, 0.1250 acres in plot No. 503 and 0.1500 acres in plot No. 502 in total = 0.4450 acres of land to Hajee Al-Helal Uddin by sale-deed No. 7115 dated 23-7-1969; that against the aforesaid sale, the SA recorded owner Hossain Uddin filed Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1970 in the First Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka and the said case was allowed in favour of Hossain Uddin by judgment dated 7-1-1978; that thereafter Hossain Uddin transferred 0.2950 acres in favour of Hajee Haider Ali by two sale-deeds being Nos. 805 and 850 both dated 7-1-1978; that out of total area 0.4450 acres, Hajee Haider Ali transferred 4 kathas of land out of plot Nos. 502 and 503 to Md Ibrahim and Julekha Begum vide four sale-deeds being Nos. 8403, 8404, 8405 and 8406 all dated 8-3-1979 and delivered possession; that Md Ibrahim and Julekha Begum then transferred 2(two) kathas of land and remained in possession over the rest 2(two) kathas of land by constructing semi-pucca building and had been in possession of the said property through tenants; that subsequently they executed a registered power-of-attorney No. 11925 dated 3-8-1997 and appointed Md Haider Ali as their constituted attorney; that thereafter constituted attorney Haider Ali transferred 2(two) kathas of land in favour of the plaintiffs by sale-deed No. 3649 dated 11-3-1998; that plaintiffs then by determining specific boundary of the property mutated their names and after obtaining necessary permission and approval of plan from RAJUK constructed 4-storied building thereon and have been paying all sort of rents and taxes to the respective authority.

5. Further case of the plaintiffs is that father of defendant Nos. 1, 9-13 and 2-8 in collusion with each other presenting one Kartik Chandra Chakrabarty as successor of Guneshwar Sharma and Kushum Kumari Debi, who were issueless created a false power-of-attorney No. 9263 dated 7-9-1992 in favour of one Abul and Shamim Anwar; that subsequently they created false deed dated 17-12-1992 and claiming title through the said deed; that defendant No.1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 201 of 1995 in the Assistant Judge, Second Court, Dhaka impleading the predecessors of the plaintiffs and the said suit was dismissed for default on 27-8-1997; that the defendants collusively mutated their names in some parts of the suit property and when the said matter was came to the knowledge of Md Haider Ali, he filed miscellaneous case in the Office of Assistant Commission Land for cancellation of the said miscellaneous case and accordingly earlier mutation case was cancelled; that when the defendant No. 1 Achia Khatun and her husband Jasim Uddin, Rahim and Karim tried to cause mischief, damage and possess the suit land of Md Ibrahim filed Petition Case No. 1305 of 1992 and all the accused persons were convicted under sections 143/448 and 109 of the Penal Code in the said case; that the plaintiffs came to know from the officers of the Khilgaon Police Station on 16-10-2003 that Achia Khatun will take possession of the suit land through Court in connection with Title Execution Case No. 8 of 2003 pending in the Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka; that thereafter on 19-10-2003 plaintiffs through their learned advocate came to know about the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 368 of 2001 wherein the defendant No.1 as plaintiff and defendant Nos.2-13 the present defendants filed the said suit for partition and with connivance with each other by practice fraud created a solenama and on the basis of solenama the said suit was decreed in preliminary form by decree dated 31-7-2002 as well as by final decree dated 26-2-2003 without impleading the actual owner of the suit property. With these averments plaintiffs were constrained to file the present suit.

6. Defendant No. 1 Mossammat Achia Khatun contested the said suit alleging, inter alia, that Jozeshwar Sharma, Rajeshwar Sharma, Ratneshwar Sharma and Guneshwar Sharma were the owners of the suit land; that each of them were owner of 4 annas share. Subsequently Guneshwar Sharma died leaving behind his wife Kusum Kumari Debi and daughter Uzzala Rani as his heirs; that on the death of Uzzala Rani her only son Kartik Chandra Chawkraborti became owner of the suit property by registered power-of-attorney No. 9263 dated 7-9-1992 he appointed Abul And Shamim Anwar as his constituted attorney; that thereafter the said attorney transferred 0.0917 acres of land in plot Nos. 502, 0.0918 acres of land in plot No. 503, 0.1625 acres of land in plot No. 504 in total 0.3540 acres of land vide sale-deed being No. 12632 dated 17-12-1992 in favour of the different persons out of which defendant No.1 got 0.508 acres of land; that thereafter the defendant No. 1 instituted a partition suit being Title Suit No. 368 of 2001 and obtained preliminary and final decree and subsequently filed Execution Case No. 8 of 2003 for possessing of the said land. The plaintiffs are filing the present suit just to harass this defendants and they are not entitled to get any relief in the present suit and prayed for dismissal of the suit.

7. In trial Court framed following issues:

১। বর্তমান আকারে অত্র মামলা রক্ষণীয় কি?

২। নালিশী ভূমিতে বাদীর স্বত্বস্বার্থ ও দখল আছে কি?

৩। অত্র মামলাটি তামাদিতে বারিত কি?

৪। বাদী তাহার প্রার্থিত প্রতিকার পাইতে পারে কি?

8. During trial the plaintiff in support of their claim examined three witnesses including the plaintiff No. 1 as PW 1 and produced documents which was marked as Exhibit 1-15. On the contrary, the defendant No.1 only deposed in the suit as dw 1 but she did not produce single document in support of her claim.

9. The learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka after considering the evidence and materials on record dismissed the suit by the impugned judgment and decree dated 15-10-2012.

10. The plaintiffs being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 15-10-2012 file this appeal.

11. Mr Probir Neogi, learned senior Advocate with Mr Sikder Mahmudur Razi, appeared on behalf of the plaintiffs-appellants. The learned Advocate Mr Sikder Mahmudur Razi, submits that the learned Joint District Judge completely over looking and in not considering the exhibited documents erroneously dismissed the suit. He further submits that although the plaintiffs were successfully proved their title and possession in the schedule property but the learned Joint District Judge failed to appreciate such evidence and material on record illegally dismissed the suit without discussing in its true perspective. He next submits that the learned Joint District Judge while passing impugned judgment erroneously held that the deposition of PW 2 Haider Ali has got no evidentiary value since there was no prayer for taking deposition of PW 2 on commission but the learned Judge totally failed to consider that the Haider All PW 2, who was the vendee of the deeds No. 805 and 850 both dated 7-1-1978 and vendor of deed Nos. 8403, 8404, 8405 and 8406 all dated 8-3-1979, who as constituted attorney of Md Ibrahim and Julekha transferred the suit property to the plaintiff by deed No. 3649 dated 11-3-1998. Learned Joint District Judge completely overlooked the order dated 3-10-2011 by which the prayer of the plaintiff was allowed to take deposition of Haider Ali PW 2 by Advocate Commission. He also submits that the present suit was filed for declaration of title and also for declaration that the judgment and preliminary and final decree dated 31-7-2012 passed in Title Suit No. 368 of 2001 are collusive, fraudulent, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiffs, who were necessary party in the said suit but not impleaded as party. Learned Advocate submits that from the written statement as well the deposition made by the dw 1, it is evident that defendant No.1 was well aware about transfer of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land but the trial Court without considering such vital evidence, erroneously dismissed the suit. Learned Advocate further contends that defendant No. 1 filed Partition Suit No. 368 of 2001 without impleading the other co-sharers of the concerned plot and same was admitted by dw 1 in her cross-examination. In reply to the submission of the learned advocate of the defendant respondent, Mr Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate submits that under Hindu law governed by Dayabhaga school, the wife only inherited the life interest for the legal necessity.

12. Mr Goutam Kumar Roy, Advocate with Ms Lucky Begum, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendants-respondents. Mr Goutam Kumar Roy, the learned Advocate submits that the certified copies of the kabala marked without objection has not been formally proved under section 65 of the Evidence Act in the absence of prove of due execution, plaintiffs cannot acquire any title in the suit property. In support of his submission he referred to a decision reported in 47 DLR (AD) 45. He further submits that since the plaintiffs have miserably failed to prove their title, so there is no necessary to give findings on compromise decree passed in Title Suit No. 368 of 2001. He next submits that the plaintiffs did not give any explanation for filing certified copy of the plaint. He also submits that Guneshwar Sharma, original CS recorded owner died leaving wife Kusum Kumari Debi and daughter Uzzala Rani. Subsequently, Uzzala Rani died leaving Kartik Chandra Chakrabarti and since Kartik Chandra Chakrabarti inherited the property from his maternal grandfather as per Dayabhaga school of Hindu law. Defendants purchased the suit property from Kartik Chandra Chakrabarti son of Uzzala Rani. He lastly submits that the plaintiffs are to prove his own case and they will not acquired title of the suit property for the weakness of the defendants. He finally submits that the trial Court upon due consideration of the evidence and materials on record rightly dismissed the suit. Accordingly, he prayed that the appeal should be dismissed and the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court should be upheld.

13. After concluding the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the appellants, in reply learned Advocate for the respondent by referring section 65 of the Evidence Act raised a legal point that the plaintiffs have filed four documents, namely, certified copy of the sale-deed No. 7115 dated 23-7-1969 (Exhibit-1) sale-deed Nos. 805 and 850 both dated 7-1-1978 Exhibits-3 and 3-ka) and sale-deed No. 8405 dated 8-3-1979 (Exhibit-5) which are not 30 years old documents as found by the trial Court as such the plaintiffs in the absence of prove of due execution of those documents cannot acquire title in the suit property.

14. In reply Mr Sikder Mahmudur Razi, the learned Advocate by referring 65(1) of the Evidence Act, 1872 submits that secondary evidence of a documents may be given of the existence, condition on contents of a document when the original is a document of which certified copy is permitted by this Act or by any other law to be given in evidence.

15. To deal with the contentions raised by the learned Advocate for both the parties regarding the certified copy of the documents (Exhibits-1, 3, 3ka, and 5) whether those may be accepted as admissible evidences. To consider this legal aspect of the matter we like to consider some other provision of the Evidence Act. Section 74(2) of the Evidence Act speaks that public record kept in Bangladesh of private document like a sale-deed when kept in the office of sub-register to which the public generally have access falls within the category of public document and a certified copy of such document can be adduced as secondary evidence are also public documents.

16. Therefore, certified copies of sale-deeds are public documents and those may be given in the evidence in any judicial proceeding as well as for proof of contents of public documents as per section 77 of the Evidence Act. As per section 79 of the Evidence Act, the Court shall presume such certified copies to be genuine and as per section 4 of the Evidence Act clearly provides whenever it is directed by this Act that the Court shall presume a fact it shall regard such fact as proved, unless and until it is disproved. As per section 110 of the Evidence Act when the question is whether any person is owner of anything of which he is shown to be in possession, the burden of proving that he is not the owner is on the person who affirms that he is not the owner.

17. Heard the learned Advocate of both the parties, perused the judgment and decree and the exhibited documents filed by the plaintiffs and the oral evidence specially the deposition of DW 1 that is the defendant No. 1, who only contested the present suit.

18. We have meticulously read all the aforesaid section of the Evidence Act, specially section 65(f) of the Evidence Act but the trial Court totally misconstrue and misread the said provision of law and illegally dismissed the suit. In this connection reliance may be placed on the decision of our apex Court referred by the learned Advocate of both the parties reported in 47 DLR (AD) 45, wherein it has been held:

"Where a case for the reception of secondary evidence is made out under the provisions of section 65, a certified copy of a registered document become admissible in proof of the existence, condition and contents of the original document under the provision of section 57(5) of the Registration Act, but the contents of the documents may not be conclusive evidence. The production of a certified copy of a sale-deed does not, however, warrant the presumption of due execution of the original document. A party producing secondary evidence of a document is not relieved of the duty of proving the execution of the original, Even in a case where a document is exhibited without objection the Court is to be satisfied as to the execution of the document".

19. In the present case the plaintiffs have successfully proved their right, title, interest and possession over the suit land. Although defendants contested the suit by filing written statement and defendant No. 1, Mosammat Asia Khatun deposed in the suit as dw 1 without filing any documents to prove her case. In her cross-examination she categorically admitted that—

“সত্য নয় যে, বাদীগণ ১৯৯৯ সালে প্লান পাশ করিয়াছে রাজউক থেকে। পরে বলে কি করছে আমি জানি না। নালিশী জমিতে বাদীপক্ষের ৪-তলা বিল্ডিং। তার ভাগে গ্যাস, বিদ্যুৎ, পানির সংযোগ আছে। নালিশী জমি বাদীর নামে সিটি পর্চা হয়েছে। সত্য নয় যে বাদীগণ পূর্ববর্তীর অনুক্রমে ভোগদখলে আছে। তবে ঝামেলা আছে। বিশ বছর যাবৎ মামলা চলিতেছে।”

But the learned Joint District Judge upon complete misreading the evidence and materials on record and upon misconception of the relevant provisions of law of Evidence erroneously dismissed the suit.

20. It is evident that the plaintiffs to prove their case filed the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 368 of 2001 (Exhibit-14 and 14-ka). It appears from (Exhibit-14 and 14-ka) that the present defendant No.1 Mossammat Achia Khatun wife of Nuruzzaman filed Partition Suit being No. 368 of 2001 impleading one Hossain for partition of their ejamli land and got preliminary decree on 31-7-2002 and final decree dated 26-2-2003. Defendant No.1 purchased of 3(three) kathas land including total 1(one) bigha and 7(seven) kathas land with five persons as stated in the deposition made by the dw 1. She also admitted in her cross-examination that—

“৩৬৮/০ নং মামলা বাতিলের কারনে তারা জমির দখল বুঝাইয়া দিতে চায় না। যার থেকে কিনেছে তারা জমির দখল বুঝাইয়া দেয় না। সে কারনে মামলা করেছি। ঐ মামলায় আমি নিজে বাদী ও ক্রয় দলিলে অপরজনদেরকে বিবাদী করেছি। ৫০২, ৫০৩, ৫০৪ দাগে অন্যান্যদেরকে পক্ষ আছে কেউ কেউ দখলে নাই। তাদের কি কাগজপত্র আছে তা আমি জিজ্ঞেস করি নাই। আমাদের ৭ জনের কে কোন জায়গা দখল করে এবং তাদের হোল্ডিং নম্বর আমি জানি না। সত্য নয় যে, তারা কেউ নালিশী জমিতে দখল (অঃ) বা আমার দলিল গ্রহীতাকে ঐ মামলায় স্বাক্ষী দেইযাব না। সত্য নয় যে, ৩৬৮/০১ মামলা যোগসাসিক পরে বলে জানি না। সত্য নয় যে, মামলায় যোগাযোগ ডিক্রি হাসিল করেছি।”

21. Learned Advocate for the respondents submits that Guneshwar Sharma died leaving his wife Kusum Kumari Debi and daughter Uzzala Rani. Their positive case is that Uzzala Rani died leaving only son Kartik Chandra Chawkraborti. Since Kartik Chandra Chawkraborti is the daughter son, he inherited the property from his maternal grandfather, Guneshwar Sharma as per Hindu law governed by Dayabhaga school. On the other hand, the plaintiff's case is that Guneshwar Sharma died issueless leaving his wife Kusum Kumari Debi only.

<u>22. To consider this legal aspect of the matter under the Dayabhaga school of Hindu law, whether a Hindu widow can transfer of the husband's property for her legal necessity. In this respect we can rely on the decision reported in 21 DLR 673, it has been held-that it is settled law of Dayabhaga school that the widow has only a limited interest in the estate she inherits from her deceased husband. But she can transfer only in case of legal necessity such as funeral expenses, for payment of rent taxes of the jaminder and for is to do necessity and for safety and well being of the estate.</u>

<u>23. As per commentaries 181 of the Mullah Hindu Law, 16th Edition, a widow alienate/ acquire only limited share that is life interest from her deceased husband. But a Hindu women cannot dispose of by gift or will the property whether moveable or immoveable properties obtained by inheritance from a male in all school of Hindu law as she has only limited interest and or transfer the property only for his legal necessity as it is evident from the Exhibit-1, wherein Kusum Kumari Debi sold the land to Helal Uddin for her legal necessity.</u>

24. It appears from the sale-deed No. 7115 dated 23-7-1969 (Exhibit-1) that by the said sale-deed Haji Helal Uddin got this property from Kusum Kumari Devi wife of Guneshwar Sharma. Since Hossain Uddin being a co-sharer of the land, he filed a pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1970 case (Exhibit-2) and same was allowed. Thereafter, Hossain Uddin transfered 29.50 decimals of land to Haji Haider Ali by two deeds being Nos. 805 and 850 both dated 7-1-1978 (Exhibit-3 and 3-ka). Subsequently, Haji Haider Ali transferred 4(four) kathas of land of Plot Nos. 502 and 503 to Ibrahim and Julekha Begum vide two registered sale-deeds being Nos. 8405 (Exhibit- 5) and 8406 (Exhibit-4) both dated 8-3-1979 and delivered possession. Thereafter Md Ibrahim and Julekha Begum transferred 2(two) kathas of land and remained in possession over rest 2(two) kathas of land by constructing four-storied building. Present plaintiffs claimed title of the property by way of purchase from Md Ibrahim and Julekah Begum through kabala No. 3649 dated 11-3-1998 (Exhibit-7). After purchase they mutated their names in the khatians (Exhibit-8- 8(kha) and obtaining permission/sanction from the Rajuk by sanction letter dated 9-12-1999 (Exhibit-9-9(kha) and constructed four-storied building on the suit land. Since then they have been in continuous possession, which was clearly found by the trial Court.

25. Moreover, none of the vendors did not dispute the successive transfers which starts from 1969 up to the last sale-deed dated 11-3-1998 (Exhibit-7), by which the plaintiffs purchased the suit land from their vendors, Md Ibrahim and Julekah Begum wife of Md Ibrahim.

26. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, the decisions cited and the provisions of Hindu law in respect of Hindu widow claiming interest in the property, we are of the opinion that the trial Court totally miss-appreciated and misconstrued the judgment and sole decree passed in Title Suit No. 368 of 2001 (Exhibit-14 series). Although the trial Court upon consideration of the Exhibits of the plaintiffs rightly found that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land by constructing four-storied building with the sanction and approved plan passed by Rajuk and mutated their names in the khatian and by paying rents and taxes to the respective authorities but erroneously dismissed the suit.

27. We have carefully gone through the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the respondents reported in 3 BLD 170 and 3 MLR (AD) 57 = 51 DLR (AD) 78 but those decisions have no manner of application in the present case.

28. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and the legal provision and the decision cited, we find merit in this appeal.

29. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15-10-2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 305 of 2003 dismissing the suit are hereby set aside and decreed the Title Suit No. 305 of 2003.

Send down the Lower Court Records at once.

End.
